stories.headline: India, EU & Canada unite to defend multilateralism; express concern over power politics
stories.bodyText:
India joined EU, Canada, Australia and several other countries in co-sponsoring a declaration expressing a joint commitment to multilateralism, international law, peace and prosperity, while expressing concern over escalating conflicts, trade disruption, power politics protectionism and coercion.
The declaration followed the announcement of a new initiative titled Partners for Multilateralism (P4M) on the margins of UN General Assembly that aims to make multilateral bodies more “representative, effective, legitimate and trusted” through middle-power cooperation, amid growing fragmentation and violations of international law.
Drawing attention to geopolitical tensions, conflicts and extreme competition, foreign minister S Jaishankar said multilateralism will be best served when international law, rules, and norms are scrupulously observed. He also emphasised de-risking and diversifying to mitigate the threat from choke points dominance and disruption.
Other declaration co-sponsors included Brazil, Barbados and Kenya, making P4M a diverse group of countries that bridges — unlike G7 and Brics — the gap between the West and Global South. After the co-sponsors, 16 other countries signed off on the declaration that flagged increasing use of economic interdependence as a source of leverage, disrupting trade, supply chains, investment and development finance in messages directed at both US and China.
The declaration stressed reform of multilateral institutions, including UN, to promote fair trade, prevent conflicts and protect rule of law, while backing fair, resilient, predictable and inclusive economic cooperation. The declaration said the multilateral system founded on UN Charter remained indispensable as it had helped provide a framework for peace, decolonisation, prosperity and human dignity.

 However, the declaration also said that it must now respond to a world that is more interconnected and complex, more contested and more multipolar.
As he underlined the need for multilateralism to assert itself strongly in these times, Jaishankar also pointed to the issue of terrorism. “The future of international security, of climate action and climate justice, of emerging technologies and development finance, of countering terrorism and strengthening supply chain, and of ensuring disaster resilience and preparing for pandemics, all depend on a will to cooperate.”

stories.headline: Trump bans media outlets CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
stories.deck: “I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW... and Politico... from the White House,” the U.S. President said in a Truth Social post
stories.bodyText:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday (September 18, 2026) he was banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them without specifics of reporting “fiction and lies.”
Also Read: 'You should not be here': Trump tells CNN at UN as standoff with media outlets persists
“I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW... and Politico... from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network.
He said that he might bar other media outlets from the White House.
It follows Mr. Trump’s decision in February 2025 to keep The Associated Press journalists out of the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events too small for a full press corps, in retaliation for the news outlet’s decision not to follow his lead in changing the Gulf of Mexico’s name.
The AP filed suit, and the case is ongoing.
Mr. Trump has long bristled at news coverage he sees as unfavourable to him and has a history of filing lawsuits against news organisations and lashing out at individual reporters in person or over social media.
Since returning to office, Mr. Trump has pursued legal action against The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, the BBC and other news outlets.
With AFP, Reuters, AP inputs
Published - September 19, 2026 12:58 am IST

stories.headline: 'You should not be here': Trump tells CNN at UN as standoff with media outlets persists
stories.deck: The tense moment was a stark reminder of how dramatically the bitter conflict between U.S. President Donald Trump and news outlets whose coverage he objects to as “fake news" has escalated in just a few days
stories.bodyText:
On a day of high-stakes diplomacy on the global stage, U.S. President Donald Trump began his United Nations visit by telling a prominent U.S. journalist, “You should not be here.”
“It's an honour to be here,” Mr. Trump said as he entered the UN doors on Tuesday (September 22, 2026) ahead of his speech to the General Assembly and faced Kaitlan Collins of CNN, a frequent target of his ire.
“I'm surprised that CNN is here covering me. You should not be here covering me. You said you weren't going to cover me.”
As Ms Collins noted later on air, CNN said nothing like that. The administration had banned CNN from White House grounds days earlier — along with MS NOW and Politico — and removed the network from pool duty. But CNN had been admitted into the UN as regularly credentialed media.
In any case, the tense moment was a stark reminder of how dramatically the bitter conflict between Mr. Trump and news outlets whose coverage he objects to as “fake news" has escalated in just a few days.
The current ban was the subject of a joint lawsuit filed Monday (September 21, 2026) by the three outlets, asking a judge to find the administration's move unconstitutional.
The White House had until Tuesday (September 22, 2026) to respond, and a hearing is scheduled for Wednesday (September 23, 2026) afternoon.
Later Tuesday (September 22, 2026), Mr. Trump doubled down on his remarks and said negative coverage was dangerous for the country.
Asked whether he would allow the outlets back in if the court rules against the White House, he said, “Well, it probably will, because this is a judge who's not a particularly fair judge.”
He was referring to U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, whom he appointed in 2017 and who ordered a CNN journalist's access restored in a similar case in 2018.
“So you never know,” Mr. Trump added. "I think we have a right to clean out fake news."
Mr. Trump's comments echoed others he's made since announcing the ban on Friday (September 18, 2026). He has referred to “purposely negative stories,” but cited no specific stories — only generally “fake news” — as justification for the ban.
The ban and lawsuit are part of a long-running conflict between the President — especially in his second term — and media outlets he finds unfavourable.
Mr. Trump has responded in the courtroom or with regulatory action. He's also lashed out at individual reporters in person or over social media, sometimes in strikingly personal terms — as he has with CNN's Collins, most recently in a speech at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.
On air, after her exchange with Mr. Trump on Tuesday (September 22, 2026), Ms. Collins said: “We never said we were not going to cover the President. We will do our best to cover him each and every day.”
Tuesday (September 22, 2026) began with an item missing from the daily press schedule issued by the White House: It did not list the U.S. network pool, a departure from the norm.
CNN had been the designated pool network for the President's trip to New York, according to a schedule that divides coverage of certain events between the five major networks. But Mr. Trump's ban removed it from pool duties.
The other pool members agreed, in solidarity, not to replace CNN with another network on the coverage, and further to suspend all pool coverage until further notice.
Other news outlets also took steps in solidarity. The Associated Press joined a number of news organisations, including The Washington Post and The New York Times, in a decision not to publish photographs of presidential events Monday (September 21, 2026).
It remains to be seen how long both the ban and the collective media action will continue.
In speeches and meetings on Tuesday (September 22, 2026), Mr. Trump was seen plenty by global audiences, thanks to UNTV — the official United Nations broadcast arm — and pool journalists covering other international leaders.
Meanwhile, a sign was spotted in the White House workspace: “I stand with AP, CNN, MS NOW, Politico.”
One longtime TV analyst says the lack of constant coverage will prove damaging to a spotlight-loving President — which may be one reason the standoff ultimately ends.
“This ban is not going to go on forever because he doesn't want that to happen, any more than anybody else,” said Robert Thompson, director of Syracuse University's Bleier Centre for Television and Popular Culture.
In the short term, Mr. Thompson said, audiences won't feel the impact in a lasting way — after all, he noted, there are many ways people get news outside of network coverage.
“We are not going to be deprived of important civic information,” Mr. Thompson said, as might have happened years ago when outlets and options were fewer.
On the other hand, if viewers were interested in what Mr. Trump said as he inaugurated a helipad at the White House on Monday (September 21, 2026), they were out of luck: The sound of Mr. Trump's whirring, waiting helicopter drowned out his remarks. TV network crews usually work to capture clearer audio.
On a deeper level, Mr. Thompson said news consumers will be impacted in a more serious way. He called out Mr. Trump's remarks labelling negative media coverage "dangerous" as troubling.
“These casual remarks, not even disguised, about what we always considered basic freedoms of the press ... that, I think, is a lot more serious,” he said.
Published - September 23, 2026 06:47 am IST

stories.headline: US warns Australia its social media reforms could ‘facilitate censorship’
stories.bodyText: The Trump administration has criticised Australia's proposed social media algorithm reforms, which would give users the option to choose the content on their feeds, warning that Washington would likely view them as "facilitating censorship".Under draft laws proposed this month by Australia's centre-left Labor government, social media platforms would be required to notify users and offer a default algorithm-recommended content feed, with the option to opt out and instead see posts only from accounts they choose to follow.In a formal submission to Australia's public consultation process, the US Embassy in Canberra said late on Tuesday it had "serious concerns" about the proposed law's goal of mandating how platforms manage content and user feeds."We are particularly concerned by potential mandates that would allow regulators to impose rigid, one-size-fits-all platform design requirements - such as forced chronological feeds or opt-in recommendation systems," the statement said.The US warned the proposed legislation could have implications beyond Australia's borders, saying the mandated algorithm design requirements "may affect what users see, say and hear not just in or from Australia, but globally."Washington urged Canberra to clearly define how "harm" and "risk" would be determined, by whom, and against what standard, cautioning that vague definitions risk enabling viewpoint-based censorship by incentivising platforms to over-moderate protected speech to avoid regulatory penalties.Should Australia compel platforms to aggressively filter algorithmic content in ways that capture protected speech, the US warned, the suppression of a disfavoured speaker or media source's reach would be no different from outright removal..‘Annihilate’ or negotiate? Trump warns Iran at UN, later confirms talks with Tehran."The US government would likely consider such a measure as facilitating censorship," the statement said.The comments come as Prime Minister Anthony Albanese attends the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where he has been promoting his government's technology reform agenda and raising concerns about the risks posed by artificial intelligence.When asked by a reporter about the US criticism of the draft legislation, Albanese said the proposed measure was not intended to grant governments greater authority, but rather to restore individuals' control over their content choices, which was reflected in the way the policy has been framed."I will always stand up for Australia's national interests, and the (reform) is something we have foreshadowed for some time," Albanese said.The Australian government is seeking feedback from digital platforms, industry bodies, civil society organisations and advocates on the draft "Digital Duty of Care" legislation, with the bill expected to be introduced to parliament this year.

stories.headline: Trump to meet Venezuela's Rodriguez for first time since Maduro's capture
stories.bodyText: US President Donald Trump will meet Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez later on Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, their first meeting since American forces captured then-President Nicolas Maduro in a January raid.The Venezuelan delegation, which includes the vice president of economy, the oil minister and officials from state oil company PDVSA, is focused on making the country look "investable," two people close to the delegation told Reuters.The pull-aside meeting, scheduled for 7:40 p.m. local time (2340 GMT) on the sidelines of a reception Trump is hosting during the UN General Assembly, comes during Rodriguez's first trip to the US since taking office. She is expected to address the General Assembly on Wednesday afternoon.Trump has built a working relationship with Rodriguez, who served as Maduro's vice president. But critics say Washington has sidelined the opposition led by Maria Corina Machado, dropping demands for free elections in favor of oil and investment deals with the interim government. A small group of Venezuelans protested in New York on Tuesday, calling for elections.In his speech to the General Assembly on Tuesday morning, Trump called Maduro an "outlaw dictator," said hundreds of political prisoners had been freed since his capture and held up the raid as proof the US would use its "unmatched military might" to protect its interests in the Western Hemisphere."To the victor belong the spoils," he said, calling an oil deal his administration signed with Caracas last month "perhaps the biggest deal ever made." Trump has said he wants $100 billion in investment to flow into Venezuela's oil industry.Rodriguez arrived in New York on Monday with a delegation that has been holding talks on energy, mining and debt with US officials, multilateral lenders and companies, according to sources. The head of the Inter-American Development Bank is working to secure approval for a $2.5 billion loan for Venezuela but has faced pushback from some members of the lender's board..‘Annihilate’ or negotiate? Trump warns Iran at UN, later confirms talks with Tehran.DEMONSTRATORS DEMAND FREE ELECTIONSEarlier on Tuesday, more than 50 protesters gathered outside the UN to protest Rodriguez's presence, waving Venezuelan flags and carrying signs reading "No Vote No Oil" and "New Face, Same Regime." Many said they wanted Trump to push for free elections in the South American country.The protesters sang the Venezuelan national anthem and chanted "Delcy, I swear, you're going to Brooklyn with Maduro" — a reference to the federal jail in the New York City borough of Brooklyn, just across the East River from the UN, where her predecessor is being held pending trial on drug trafficking charges."On one hand, it's outrageous to see part of the regime meeting with the authorities of this country's current government, but there's also no doubt that thanks to this government, today we are one step closer to freedom," said Miguel Eduardo Martinez, a 34-year-old social media manager who moved from Caracas in 2017."Delcy Rodriguez wasn't born on January 3, 2026. Delcy Rodriguez has been with the Chavista dictatorship for more than 20 years. She has been complicit," said Cesar Coello, who carried a sign depicting Rodriguez in an orange jumpsuit. Chavismo is the political movement founded by the late Venezuelan President Hugo Chávez.Coello said he hoped Trump and Rodriguez would discuss holding elections soon.

briefs.headline: Lack of hygienic menstrual shelters posing health risk to tribal women
briefs.deck: There is only one valaimpura serving approximately 100 women and adolescent girls, and its condition is pathetic
briefs.bodyText:
The absence of a modern, hygienic rest facility for Muthuvan tribal women during menstruation has created a severe health hazard in the Lakkam tribal settlement near Munnar. According to M. Palraj, president of the Adivasi Muthuvan Samudhaya Sangam, the community’s traditional secluded huts —known locally as ‘valaimpura’ — are in deplorable condition, leaving women and young girls afraid to stay there.
“Nearly 80 families reside in the Lakkam settlement under Munnar panchayat. There is only one valaimpura serving approximately 100 women and adolescent girls, and its condition is pathetic. During rains, water leaks directly inside the shelter,” said Mr. Palraj.
Under Muthuvan customary practice, women and girls are strictly segregated to a valaimpura for seven days during their menstrual cycle. Compelled by tradition to stay in these unsanitary and insecure quarters, residents face significant health risks and distress. Community leaders noted a sharp contrast between shelters designated for men and those for women.
While the Sathram—a communal shelter built by the Vana Samrakshana Samithi (VSS) where unmarried young men reside until marriage—remains in good condition, the women’s facility has been left neglected.
Isolation practice
The isolation practice previously made headlines in 2017 when a report by the tribal intelligence wing revealed that inadequate valaimpura facilities in Edamalakkudy, Keralam’s first tribal grama panchayat, had driven some adolescent girls to take oral contraceptive pills to delay their menstrual cycles.
Recently, conditions improved in Edamalakkudy after an IT firm, Experion Technologies, built two modern rest facilities called “Women’s Empowerment Centres” under its CSR initiative, Project EDEM. Lakkam residents are now urging authorities to construct a similar model facility in their settlement.
Compounding the community’s isolation is the dilapidated 4-km stretch of road linking the settlement to the Munnar–Udumalpet interstate highway near Lakkam Waterfalls. Addressing the issue, Idukki district panchayat Munnar Division member C. Nelson stated that ₹10 lakh each has been allocated for both the road and the valaimpura construction. “The tender for the valaimpura has already been awarded, but the contractor has not yet commenced work,” Mr Nelson said. “A recurring hurdle across tribal settlements in Idukki, including Edamalakkudy, is that outside contractors secure tenders online but fail to show up or execute the ground work,” he said.
Published - September 23, 2026 07:04 am IST

briefs.headline: Cong accuses BJP of Assam attack, CM blames party’s ‘internal feud’
briefs.bodyText:
GUWAHATI/NEW DELHI: Two Congress functionaries were injured and several vehicles damaged in Assam Monday after an alleged attack on their convoy in Samaguri where they were campaigning for the Oct 6 Nagaon assembly bypoll.
AICC secretary Manoj Chouhan and Assam Mahila Congress president Mira Borthakur were injured in the incident in Nagaon district. AICC in-charge of Assam, Bhupesh Baghel, was also part of the roadshow. Congress later filed an FIR at Nagaon and sought adequate security for Baghel.
Assam Congress’s media department chairperson Bedabrata Bora alleged “hired BJP goons” attacked the convoy with bottles, stones and bricks. He said Chouhan suffered chest and abdominal injuries, while Borthakur sustained head injuries.
Around four vehicles, including those carrying LS MP Gaurav Gogoi and candidate Sibamoni Bora, were severely damaged, he said.
Baghel Tuesday blamed CM Himanta Biswa Sarma for the attack. “The attack was nothing but a manifestation of Sarma’s panic. They have already conceded defeat and are desperately trying to intimidate us into retreating indoors.

Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
But he should know we are not people who can be frightened,” he said.
In Delhi, Congress held a presser to denounce the “planned murderous attack”.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh posted on X that it was a “shameful attempt by BJP, with the tacit approval of Election Commission, to avert a likely defeat” in the bypoll.
The Assam chief minister denied BJP’s involvement and blamed the incident to internal Congress rivalry. “There is constant dispute and infighting between them,” he said.

briefs.headline: Pakistan must act against cross-border terrorism before world believes it would do what it says: MEA
briefs.deck: India, after the Pahalgam attack last year, has maintained that Islamabad should credibly and irrevocably abjure its support for cross-border terrorism
briefs.bodyText:
Pakistan must take "credible action" against cross-border terrorism before the world believes Islamabad would do what it says, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Tuesday (September 22, 2026).
During his bi-weekly briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked how New Delhi viewed the comments by Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces, Field Marshal Asim Munir, who said the armed forces were determined to defeat terrorism amid the rising threat of militancy in the country.
"Pakistan needs to demonstrate action and firm commitment. And it must take credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world believes it would do what it says," he said.
India, after the Pahalgam attack last year, has maintained that Islamabad should credibly and irrevocably abjure its support for cross-border terrorism.
Field Marshal Munir earlier in the day said Pakistan's armed forces are determined to defeat terrorism amid the rising threat of militancy in the country.
The field marshal visited Corps Headquarters in Peshawar, where he interacted with senior officers and was briefed on the prevailing security situation in the province, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).
He was also briefed on the ongoing counter-terrorism operations, border management measures and operational preparedness of formations deployed in the province.
"He emphasised that the Armed Forces, with the unwavering support of the nation, remain resolute in their determination to defeat terrorism and ensure lasting peace and stability across the country," according to the Pakistan Army.
Field Marshal Munir also paid tribute to those who laid down their lives in the fight against terrorism.
Read | It is not all bad between India and Pakistan
Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil -- particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) -- that are used for attacks in Pakistan.
Afghanistan, however, denies allowing its territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.
India on Tuesday (September 22, 2026) also strongly condemned airstrikes carried out by Pakistan in parts of Afghanistan and said "such instances of aggression" against a sovereign neighbour are something that vitiates regional peace and security.
Mr. Jaiswal said this in response to a query during the bi-weekly media briefing.
Pakistan on Monday (September 21, 2026) said its security forces carried out airstrikes on terrorist camps and hideouts in the border region with Afghanistan, killing 28 terrorists, including multiple suicide bombers.
Mr. Jaiswal was also asked to comment on reports that Pakistan has made a fresh claim in connection with a recent pronouncement by a "Court of Arbitration (CoA)" linked with the Indus Waters Treaty.
"Regarding the 'permanent court' or so-called 'Permanent Court of Arbitration', I would like to say that Pakistan has a habit of misrepresenting facts and propagating falsehoods to serve its malicious propaganda.
"For starters, the so-called ruling is not a ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration, as sought to be projected by the Pakistan minister. It is a ruling by an illegally constituted court. We see this as just another attempt by Pakistan at distorting reality. Our position on this issue is very clear, and we have reiterated it several times," Mr. Jaiswal said.
Published - September 23, 2026 07:03 am IST

briefs.headline: Prominent citizens oppose AIMPLB's Shariat campaign
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: More than 90 citizens, who identify themselves as progressive Muslim activists, intellectuals and women's rights advocates, have strongly opposed what they cited as the "ill-conceived" nationwide 'Save India, Save Shariat' campaign launched by All India Muslim Personal Law Board (
AIMPLB
) last week.
In a statement, they have called upon all progressive forces, civil society organisations and secular political parties to intervene actively to ensure that the demand for a gender-just, religion-neutral 
Uniform Civil Code

Ratna Pathak, Javed Anand and Feroze Mithiborwala (Indian Muslims for Secular Democracy-IMSD), Zakia Soman and Noorjahan Safia Niaz (Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan-BMMA), Shamsuddin Tamboli (Muslim Satyashodhak Mandal) and Bader Saeed (Roshni). briefs.headline: National film awards will now be at tourist destinations: Ashwini Vaishnaw
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: On a day Ekta Nagar in Gujarat's Kevadia - where '
Statue of Unity
' holds centrestage - became the space for at the 72nd National Film Awards, information and broadcasting minister 
Ashwini Vaishnaw
 on Tuesday said govt plans to take these awards to some of the best tourism destinations across states in the future.
He urged all states to send in their proposals of best tourist destinations, and prepare and execute 360 degree development plans in those areas. "The proposal of whichever state is selected, the next national film awards will be held at that tourist destination," he said.
Reflecting on PM Narendra Modi's vision when G20 summit was organised in India in 2023, Vaishnaw said that at that time too programmes related to the summit were held across different states. The same is being done with the film awards and, therefore, these are being organised and will be taken to different tourist destinations in the future, he said.

briefs.headline: Macron urges world to choose UN over ‘law of the jungle’
briefs.deck: ‘What is our credibility worth if we remain inactive on Gaza; some claim that peace has been achieved, but this has not opened up humanitarian deliveries; it is a spectacle that shames us all,’ said Emmanuel Macron
briefs.bodyText:
French President Emmanuel Macron called Tuesday (September 22, 2026) for countries to recommit to international laws and the UN system over a resurgent "law of the jungle."
Mr. Macron, giving his last speech to the UN's signature annual diplomatic gathering as president, also railed against the humanitarian situation in Gaza while calling for a moratorium on strikes against civilian and energy targets in the Ukraine-Russia war.
"The question put to us, in very simple terms, is whether we want to live in this state of nature, with a kind of return to the law of the jungle, or in a civilized international society," he said.
"My message is to stand firm. Do not yield to the situation which is developing...The rhetoric of defeat that is giving way to abuse of power by empires, threatening the sovereignty of some nations," Mr. Macron said.
The French President, who has been a stalwart supporter of Ukraine and raised the country's case in a meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday (September 21), called for Moscow and Kyiv to agree to a moratorium on striking civilian and energy targets.
‘Barbaric acts’
"We've seen the destruction of civilian infrastructure, human rights violations. It's a new era of barbaric acts," he said.
"We must protect the civilian population, and this is why we'd like to express our support for a double moratorium, a moratorium on strikes on energy and civilian infrastructure," he added.
He also raised the plight of the Palestinian people in Gaza.
"What is our credibility worth if we remain inactive on Gaza? Some claim that peace has been achieved, but this has not opened up humanitarian deliveries. It is a spectacle that shames us all," he said.
Following several other leaders at the UN rostrum who had raised alarm about the risks posed by artificial intelligence, Mr. Macron proposed an alternative architecture for its development.
"I don't want anyone to become the vassal of one of the great powers. Rather, we must come together to build an open-source frontier model, a cutting-edge model," he told the UN General Assembly, apparently in reference to AI powerhouses China and the U.S.
"Our investment capabilities must be pooled to build a cutting-edge open-source AI model, which we will share. We should not depend on somebody else."
Published - September 23, 2026 03:22 am IST

briefs.headline: 'Democracy chori,' says BJP citing HC order on Sonia case
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Attacked by 
Congress
 for "vote chori", 
BJP
 Tuesday latched on to a Delhi court order to charge its rival with "democracy chori" and asked 
Rahul Gandhi
 to respond to allegation that Sonia Gandhi had cast her vote in 1980 even before she accepted Indian citizenship.
BJP's offensive came a day after a Delhi court set aside a magistrate's order refusing to probe the allegation that Sonia's name was included in the poll rolls three years before she acquired Indian citizenship in 1983. briefs.headline: ED searches office of senior Punjab official over building scam
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: In a crackdown on a nexus of senior officials of Punjab govt and builders relating to Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (Gmada), ED Tuesday searched multiple premises in Delhi, Ludhiana, Panchkula, Mohali and Chandigarh, including the office of Gmada and that of IAS officer and principal secretary (housing and urban development) Vikas Garg.
It is probing senior officials of Punjab govt and several builders and developers in connection with alleged corruption in Gmada and for the award of projects to builders through auction, waiver of external development charges, interest charges, etc.
Searches were conducted on 26 premises “related to Tirupati Infraprojects Pvt Ltd and its promoters, directors and associated persons, besides others”. The other builders under probe include Remigate Buildestates (India) Pvt Ltd, MB Infrabuild Pvt Ltd, Mera Baba Reality Associates Pvt Ltd and Mera Baba Infrastructure Pvt Ltd.
“Simultaneously, searches are being conducted at the offices of Gmada and of the department of housing and urban development, Punjab, to gather evidence from the accused entities,” sources said. “Tirupati Infraprojects is also an accused in CBI and ED cases, being allegedly involved in a bank fraud to the tune of Rs 290 crore concerning a project, Radisson Blu hotel, at Paschim Vihar, New Delhi.”

“Investigation has revealed that the promoters of Tirupati Infraprojects also control entities Remigate Buildestates (India), MB Infrabuild, which had acquired two prime auction sites at Mohali from Gmada and thereafter obtained substantial financial relief in respect of the dues payable to the authority,” an official said.
ED has estimated suspected undue gain to the firms and the loss to the exchequer at more than Rs 100 crore. ED is also searching a consultancy firm, Tila Consultants & Contractors, which deals with various consultancy works of Gmada and is suspected to have acted as an intermediary in the scam.

stories.headline: Karnataka rejects Ghats report, seeks 1-year survey window
stories.deck: Karnataka's legislature adopted a resolution rejecting the Centre's seventh draft Ecologically Sensitive Area notification. Chief Minister DK Shivakumar emphasized the need for a one-year ground survey to classify land accurately. The resolution demanded the exclusion of agricultural lands and settlements from eco-sensitive designations. Concerns were raised regarding the potential economic…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Karnataka legislature Tuesday unanimously adopted a resolution rejecting the Centre’s seventh draft Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA) notification. The resolution followed a discussion, held in both the assembly and council, on the Kasturirangan report on the Western Ghats.
Moved by chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
, the resolution seeks a one-year window from the Centre for a ground-level survey to separate forests from farms, plantations and human settlements before the notification is finalised.
Shivakumar announced a committee headed by a retired judge, with revenue and forest officials, farmer associations, industrialists and ecology experts on the panel, to address the draft’s shortcomings.
The resolution adopted by Karnataka objected to the inclusion of agricultural land, plantations, homes and public utility spaces alongside forested areas under ESA. It also flagged a lack of precise demarcation of land, calling it unscientific to declare an entire village as ESA merely because a fifth of it fell within forest limits.
“Forests must be protected and people of the Western Ghats have done so for generations. 
They should not face hurdles or threats,” the CM said, adding that a delegation would soon travel to Delhi to press the region’s case.
Claiming that the draft offered no economic assistance to or alternative livelihood for affected people, the resolution urged the Centre to exclude farmland, plantations, settlements and public-use spaces from ESA.
Responding to a question from opposition leader R Ashok on the 
National Green Tribunal
’s directives, Shivakumar said senior advocates would be appointed to present Karnataka’s stand before the 
Supreme Court
 on the Centre’s Kasturirangan report notification.
The CM clarified that the state was not disrespecting the Kasturirangan committee’s recommendations, but wanted those scientifically revised in Karnataka’s interest, adding that since drone surveys tend to show the entire topography as green, a survey through the revenue department was needed.
When MLAs cutting across party lines flagged unresolved issues, including Bagar Hukum, forest rights, deemed forests, land grants and pending court cases, Shivakumar assured those would be taken up separately.
BOX:‘Beware, forest dept is watching’
Chief minister DK Shivakumar cautioned against encroachment upon forest land and poaching of wild animals, saying improved surveillance had made evasion harder, with cameras now tracking both trespassers as well as animal movements.
Urging people to surrender their hunting guns, he said the govt had given them enough time to comply with the norms. Any violation now will lead to police action. “Please surrender them [hunting weapons]. You do not need them. Let us see how many come forward,” he said.
OPTIONAL BOX:What the Centre’s draft says
The draft, issued on July 27, earmarks 20,668 sq km across 33 taluks and 1,449 villages in 10 Western Ghats districts under ESA category. The 10 districts are Belagavi, Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu, Hassan, Uttara Kannada, Dakshina Kannada, Mysuru, Shivamogga and Udupi.
This is part of a larger plan covering 56,000 sq km across six states.
States had 60 days to file objections to the draft proposal.
Points for infogfx:ESA REJECTION MATRIX
* K’taka seeks one-year survey window for ground-level survey
* Demands exclusion of farmlands, plantations, and homes from ESA limits
* Objects to marking entire villages as eco-sensitive based on partial forest cover
* Flags draft as unscientific owing to zero economic aid for affected residents

stories.headline: Haifa day: Deterioration of memorial in Basra distresses families of martyrs
stories.deck: The Mysore Lancers, the armed force of the erstwhile Mysore princely State, was part of the Indian Expeditionary Force, which troops from other princely States were a part of.
stories.bodyText:
The deterioration of the Basra War Memorial in conflict-hit Iraq has caught the attention of those who are aware of the history of the Mesopotamian Campaign in World War I (1914–1921) and also of the families that lost their dear ones. The memorial was built for the 40,500 service personnel from the Commonwealth who died in the war. A large number of them were Indians, and many were from the Mysore Imperial Lancers, whose exploits in WWI, especially in the liberation of Haifa, have been etched in the annuls of modern warfare.
As the Haifa Liberation Day is observed worldwide, including at the Haifa Memorial in Bengaluru on Wednesday (September 23), those chronicling the sacrifice of the Mysore Lancers have expressed grief over the recent disclosures in the United Kingdom that revealed destruction to tombstones.
“Recent information shows destruction of at least 3,000 tombstones in Basra. Campaigns by families of deceased soldiers are now seeking public help in collecting further evidences of destruction,” said journalist Anil Raje Urs, who recently released his book ‘Mysore Lancers - Valour in the World War I’, in which he traces the Lancers’ journey and exploits in West Asia’s deadly battle fields of WWI.
The Mysore Lancers, the armed force of the erstwhile Mysore princely State, was part of the Indian Expeditionary Force, which troops from other princely States were a part of. Initially deployed to guard the critical Suez Canal in 1915-17, they were part of war efforts later, participating in several conflicts with the Ottoman and German forces in Mesopotamia (modern-day Iraq), Jerusalem, Gaza and Haifa.
The exploits of Mysore Lancers in the Liberation of Haifa on September 23, 1918, is seen in the context of modern warfare in which the Lancers overcame the Ottomans and Germans. “The troops from Mysore were without any modern weapons. They were sent to attack the Turks who were perched in Mt. Carmel with their machine guns and naval guns. With their raw courage, they braved the heavy machine gun fire to silence the Turks,” said Mr. Urs, related to late Col. J. Desraj Urs, the commander of Mysore Lancers in WW I. The Indian forces, including the Mysore Lancers, were involved in the rescue of Abdu’l-Baha, the eldest son of Baha’u’llah, the founder of Baha’I faith at Haifa.
Mr. Urs’s book in Kannada traces interesting information, sourced from palace records, on the preparation before the Mysore Lancers left for West Asia. “With available records, I was able to trace about 15 families whose members had taken part in WWI. Many more are yet to be traced,” said the author.
Despite the public acknowledgement of the contribution of Mysore Lancers, the Basra war memorial did not have accurate details of a large number of Indian soldiers. The Commonwealth War Grave Commission also acknowledges it. The Commission’s website says that names of most of the men of the Indian Army who it commemorates were not accurate since war records at the time had not been properly compiled. Since then an accurate list of names has been compiled in the CWGC’s Iraq Roll of Honour in the U.K., waiting for a time when condition on the ground allow a more permanent solution.

stories.headline: 10km ride, nearly 2 hours on the road every day for schoolkids in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
TRAPPED IN TRAFFIC: As school bus speeds drop, brisk walkers outpace them; Thursdays the worst commute day
A grade 7 student's drawing of daily commute -- girdlock, honking, missed meals, and an unwell child
Traffic mess on Whitefield-Sarjapur road — the city’s showcase corridor that hosts marquee tech companies — has increased a 10km school commute time from 92 minutes in 2024-25 to 112 minutes in 2026-27. This means nearly two hours is spent in metal containers called school buses.
School buses on this east Bengaluru road are clocking an average speed of 9.2kmph. For perspective, as per data from TomTom Traffic Index (the annual analysis of global traffic trends and commuting behaviour), the average speed during rush hour in Bengaluru in 2025 was 13.9kmph.
Analysis of GPS data from 61 school buses of Inventure Academy near Dommasandra Circle shows that students are spending nearly two hours a school day travelling to and from school. Over 200 school days, that works out to 374 hours — equivalent to nearly 53 school days spent on the road.
The area has 42 private schools and more than 1,000 school buses, according to the school’s mapping, potentially affecting around 40,000 students travelling by school bus.
Thank God It’s Not Thursday
Morning travel time on this stretch has increased from 39 to 47 minutes, while evening travel time has jumped from 53 to 65 minutes. 
Thursdays are the worst: afternoon travel between the school and Varthur Kodi averages 76 minutes, with buses moving at only 8.4kmph. Tuesday is relatively better at 59 minutes, while Wednesday averages 68 minutes.
The slowest stretch is towards Prestige Lakeside Habitat and Palm Meadows, where buses average just 6.4kmph — the average speed of brisk walkers. Routes towards Gran Carmen, Adarsh Palm Retreat, and AECS Layout-Kundalahalli fare somewhat better at 11.3kmph.
“During peak hours, traffic along this corridor can move extremely slowly, significantly increasing students’ commute time. Walking is not a practical alternative, given the lack of footpaths and concerns around safety and exposure to pollution,” the school said.
And delays are becoming routine. About 60% of trips arrive after their scheduled time, 15% are delayed by at least 30 minutes, and 4% of buses run an hour late.
Multiple bottlenecks are feeding the traffic mess. Buses heading towards Whitefield pass through Gunjur Temple and Double Road diversion, while the temporary closure of Club Road has pushed more traffic onto the already congested route. Those heading towards Sarjapur Road via SH-35 face an incomplete flyover, damaged roads and potholes.
Eventually, buses from different routes converge on the same constrained 10km stretch between Dommasandra Circle and Varthur Kodi.
“Some 86% of our students travel by school bus. While schools are doing their part to optimise school transport, govt must ensure basic road infrastructure and more efficient traffic management. Our analysis highlights how data and technology can enable smarter planning. For instance, Thursdays are consistently the worst for traffic. Could more offices allow employees to work from home that day, or stagger office timings so that schools and workplaces are not all putting vehicles on the road at the same time?” said Nooraine Fazal, founder of Inventure Academy.
LOCATION-SPECIFIC INTERVENTIONSFive critical bottlenecks require defined intervention, clear responsibility and visible completion timeline.1. DOMMASANDRA CIRCLE* Specific challenge:
 Broken roads, potholes and incomplete flyover work reduce usable road space width and disrupt junction movement
* Location-specific action:
 Repair damaged stretches; complete priority flyover work; introduce a junction-specific traffic-flow plan
2. GUNJUR* Specific challenge: High traffic volumes converge on narrow roads; the temporary Club Road closure adds further pressure
* Location-specific action: Managemovement at turnings and school-hour traffic flow; deploy personnel at choke points; review diversions
3. VARTHUR KODI* Specific challenge:
 Narrow and encroached roads, diversions and conflicting traffic movements create sustained congestion
* Location-specific action: Clear obstructions; repair diversion routes; introduce scientifically planned junction cycles during peak hours
4. VIBGYOR ROAD – KUNDALAHALLI* Specific challenge: Poor road condition and waterlogging reduce usable road space, especially during and after rain
* Location-specific action: Resurface damaged stretches; address drainage; strengthen school-hour traffic management
5. GRAN CARMEN* Specific challenge: Broken roads, weak signal management and the U-turn arrangement disrupt traffic flow
* Location-specific action:
 Repair damaged stretches; recalibrate signal timings; provide a dedicated U-turn bay or relocate the median opening.
-- Source: Inventure Academy

stories.headline: Kasturirangan report could force Uttara Kannada families to migrate to Goa: Karnataka Assembly Deputy Speaker
stories.bodyText:
Legislative Assembly Deputy Speaker Mankal Vaidya on Tuesday said the people of Uttara Kannada had made enormous sacrifices for development projects in the district and would be forced to migrate to neighbouring Goa if the State failed to protect their interests in dealing with the Kasturirangan report.
Mr. Vaidya, who represents the Bhatkal Assembly constituency, said more than half of the district’s 14 lakh population lived in the Western Ghats region and could be affected if the report was implemented in its present form.
Participating in the debate in the Assembly on the report’s implications for livelihoods, he said the people had given up large tracts of land for several major projects, including the Konkan Railway, Seabird naval base, Kaiga Nuclear Power Station, five hydel projects and national highways. Nearly 21,000 acres had been acquired for the Seabird project alone, he said.
If the Kasturirangan recommendations were implemented in their present form, towns such as Bhatkal, Sirsi, and Honnavar would be affected, and more than 85,000 families could face displacement, Mr. Vaidya said. “We will have to move either to the 13 islands or to Goa,” he said.
A State Cabinet meeting held in Mangaluru last week proposed to develop tourism in 13 islands on the State’s coast.
Urging the state government to oppose the recommendations before the National Green Tribunal, Mr. Vaidya said the people of Uttara Kannada deserved justice. “Because of multiple projects and now the Kasturirangan report, no one is living with happiness in the district,” he said.
He also questioned the contribution of the Forest Department to forest conservation, saying farmers and local communities had traditionally protected forests while sharing fruits and vegetables from their farms with wildlife. Farmers were losing a significant portion of their coconut and jackfruit produce because of crop damage caused by wildlife, he said.
BJP member S. Suresh Kumar suggested that the Chief Ministers of all six Western Ghats States meet and arrive at a unanimous position on implementing the recommendations. With the population of the region declining, several houses in the coastal and Malnad areas had effectively become old-age homes, he said, stressing the need to protect local livelihoods.

briefs.headline: Heavy vehicles barred during school hours on key Bengaluru stretch
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: With children spending precious school hours stuck in traffic on the Varthur-Gunjur stretch (SH-35) in east Bengaluru, traffic police have imposed additional restrictions on the movement of heavy vehicles.
Heavy goods vehicles will now be restricted from entering the corridor from 7-11am, 1-3pm, and 4-9pm, covering key morning and evening peak-hour periods as well as school bus movement timings. Previously, heavy vehicles were barred between 7am and 11am.
Officials said the new restrictions were introduced following complaints over worsening traffic on the busy corridor. Police said the restrictions will remain in force until the traffic situation improves substantially.
“The road is narrow and has multiple T-junctions. Until traffic movement normalises and the road is widened to handle the current volume, these restrictions will continue,” an official added.
According to Whitefield traffic police, the movement of heavy vehicles on the state highway contributes significantly to bottlenecks, particularly at junctions and other choke points along the corridor. “This is a state highway and naturally sees a high volume of heavy vehicle movement. However, considering the present road conditions, traffic volume and movement of schoolchildren, a decision was taken to restrict heavy vehicles during additional afternoon and evening slots as well,” a police officer told 
TOI
.
The officer acknowledged that while enforcement teams have been stopping trucks and other heavy vehicles at entry points during restricted hours, some vehicles entered the corridor before the restrictions took effect.

briefs.headline: Family at hospital, thieves break into Bengaluru home and steal 500 grams of gold
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A house in Vivekananda Nagar, Electronics City, whose occupants had been away for two days attending to their ailing son, was burgled after miscreants broke open the front door and made away with gold jewellery weighing 450-500 grams.
According to a complaint filed by Ebanezer V, a private firm employee, he admitted his younger son to a private hospital on Sept 17 for treatment. He and his wife then stayed at the hospital to care for him.
On the morning of Sept 19, his elder son returned home to collect his shuttlecock and racket, locked the house and took the key with him before staying at a friend’s house.
The following morning, around 8.30am, Ebanezer’s wife returned home to freshen up but was shocked to find the front door ajar. She immediately informed her husband, who rushed home and inspected the house.
The lock on the main door had been broken, while boxes containing jewellery kept inside an iron almirah in the bedroom were found scattered on the floor. The family had kept several gold ornaments, including necklaces, gold chains, bracelets, bangles, earrings and finger rings.
However, the complainant said he was yet to ascertain the exact weight and value of the stolen jewellery. 
He told police he would consult his wife after she returned from the hospital and provide the precise details.
A case has been registered under BNS Sections 305 (theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship) and 331 (house-trespass or housebreaking). CCTV footage from surrounding buildings and roads is being analysed for clues about the burglars.

briefs.headline: Karnataka high court defers plea on Vande Mataram order
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Karnataka high court Tuesday deferred hearing on a PIL plea challenging the state govt’s order restricting the singing of 
Vande Mataram
 to its first two stanzas at govt programmes, except those attended by the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister or Governor.
Advocate Girish Bharadwaj has challenged the Sept 8 order.
A division bench of Justices Anu Sivaraman and TP Vivekananda noted that the 
Supreme Court
 is considering a challenge to the constitutional validity of the 2026 amendment to the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, which criminalises insults to Vande Mataram. The bench said the SC’s decision would directly affect the PIL and deferred the matter.
The petitioner alleged the state decision violated a Centre directive. The petitioner contended that the state cabinet took the decision without a cabinet note or legal opinion and added that the state govt could not have reduced the six-stanza national song into two stanzas.
The advocate general said Vande Mataram was optional, while additional solicitor general Aravind Kamath said the amendment gave it status similar to the national anthem.

briefs.headline: ITBP personnel dies in road accident in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A 46-year-old member of 
Indo-Tibetan Border Police
 (ITBP) succumbed to injuries after his motorbike rammed into a wrongly parked tractor by the side of the road near Kanakapura in Ramanagara late Monday night.
The deceased is DS Channaveeragowda, a resident of Shivanahalli village in Kanakapura. According to police, Channaveeragowda, who was stationed in Belagavi, had come home on a fortnight’s leave on Sunday.
On Monday night, Channaveeragowda and his minor son were riding from Shivanahalli to Kanakapura when the accident took place, police said. “Channaveeragowda’s family has built a new house in Kanakapura town. He and his 14-year-old son were riding back to town for dinner when his motorbike rammed into the tractor from behind. Other commuters on the road called us and when we reached the spot, the tractor driver had escaped with the vehicle. Channaveeragowda was shifted to a private hospital, where he died early Tuesday morning,” an investigating officer said.

briefs.headline: From stage to strings: Bengaluru artists head to Indonesia for puppet festival
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Two Bengaluru-based theatrepersons will represent the city at an international biennale puppet festival in Indonesia from Sept 25 to Oct 11.
Theatre-maker Gagan Prasad and theatre practitioner Joseph John were selected through an international open call. They are among 12 artists participating in Puppet Camp, part of Pesta Boneka #10, to be held at Yogyakarta. The event is hosted by Papermoon Puppet Theatre.
“This is deeply encouraging. It is an opportunity to take my work from Bengaluru to a completely new creative environment, while also learning from artists and traditions I have not had an opportunity to work with before,” said Gagan, a resident of Padmanabhanagar in south Bengaluru.
For Gagan, the journey into puppetry has been years in the making. He founded Spashta Theatre in 2017. His interest in puppetry took root while directing his second play, Neenaanaanadare Naaneeneenaa, an adaptation of Shakespeare’s The Comedy of Errors.
John, who has over 38 years of experience in theatre and is from Kerala, has been part of Kannada theatre after graduating from Neenasam, a repertory in Shivamogga district. 
He trained in puppetry in Dehradun and is a writer and actor in Kannada and Malayalam films.
“It is a very famous group and participants from many countries come there. This is a rare opportunity for me,” John said.
The programme will feature a masterclass by US-based puppeteer Tom Lee on Kuruma Ningyō, a traditional Japanese puppetry form. Gagan and the other artists will collaborate with Yara Arts Group (US) and Hachioji Kuruma Ningyō, The Koryu Nishikawa Troupe (Japan), to develop Shank’s Mare, which will be presented at the festival.

briefs.headline: Coalition publishes Kannada translation of seventh ESA draft to bridge information gap for local communities
briefs.deck: Despite the largest share of the proposed protected area being in Karnataka, the officials have not made the draft available in Kannada, and it is available only in English and Hindi
briefs.bodyText:
A coalition of organisations has published a Kannada translation of the seventh draft notification on the Western Ghats Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA), given that the draft is currently available only in Hindi and English.
The draft, which aims to restrict destructive activities in the ecologically fragile Western Ghats, was published by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in July inviting comments and objections from the public.
Despite the largest share of the proposed protected area being in Karnataka, the draft has not been made available in Kannada, thereby limiting the understanding of a large section of the State on what the draft proposes.
The Kannada translation of the proposed policy was published by the coalition to bridge this information gap.
Information gap
“People are being asked to respond to a notification they cannot read,” said Nirmala Gowda, from Mapping Malnadu which is part of the coalition.
In Karnataka, the Directorate of Translations is responsible for translating Central and State legislations, Acts, and Rules into Kannada.
The coalition members point out that despite having an institutional mechanism for translation in place, the State government has not made the notification available to the public in Kannada even after more than a decade passed since the Kasturirangan report came out.
Following the draft notification, there is widespread public sentiment against it, especially in places such as Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru and Uttara Kannada, where people fear that it would result in their displacement and hit their livelihood.
“Currently, the narrative is being shaped by vested interests, who are spreading misinformation to mobilise support from local communities,” claimed a coalition member.
Notarised translation
As a response, the coalition has translated the draft notification, notarised it, and made it publicly available.
“We are not interpreting or explaining anything here. People can go through the translated document and take decisions,” said the member.
“As per the draft notification, mining falls under the prohibited red category of activities. There are several politicians associated with mining in the Western Ghats. Big projects like the Sharavati pump storage project, hydel projects and nuclear power projects, and construction projects with built-up area of 20,000 sq. m or more are also prohibited. But none of these will affect local communities in any way. People are being misguided,” one of the members said.
Other members of the coalition include Bengaluru Environment Forum, Federation of Shivamogga Citizens’ Welfare Forums, Forest, Environment and Climate Change Association, Friends for Future, Go Green, Green Life Shivamogga Trust, Human Rights Foundation, Jana Sangrama Parishat, Karnataka Jnana Vijnana Samiti and Karnataka Sarvodaya Mandali, N.E.C.F., Nature First, Parisara Sangama Vedike, Parisarakagi Naavu Sanghatane, Paryavarani Foundation, Rashtra Bhaktara Balaga, Saara Kendra, Sangatya, Sneha Kunja Trust, Ulivu Foundation, United Conservation Movement and Yuva Sanchalana.
This is not the first time that a lack of adequate information in regional language before finalising critical decisions around environment has been pointed out.
In August 2025, the local fishing community in Keni village in Uttara Kannada had demanded a Kannada translation of the draft Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report for a proposed commercial port by JSW in the region. While the English version of the draft report was around 600 pages, the Kannada version was only a 48-page executive summary.

briefs.headline: Karnataka HC orders court-monitored probe into KPSC irregularities; sets up SIT headed by DGP Alok Kumar
briefs.deck: While giving 100 days for the SIT to complete investigation and submit final report, the Court also directed it to submit an investigation progress report every 30 days
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka High Court on Monday ordered a court-monitored investigation — by constituting a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by senior IPS officer and Director-General of Police Alok Kumar — into the alleged large-scale irregularities in the recruitment processes conducted by the Karnataka State Public Service Commission (KPSC).
While giving 100 days for the SIT to complete the investigation and submit the final report, the court also directed it to submit an investigation progress report every 30 days.
Yatnal and others’ petition
Justice M. Nagaprasanna passed the order on petitions by Basanagouda R. Patil Yatnal, MLA, All Karnataka State Students’ Association, and Manjunath. The petitioners had sought a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into two cases: on selection of a daughter of the KPSC’s suspended chairperson Shivashankar S. Sahukar to the post of Industrial Extension Officer; and alleged illegalities in the process of selection of candidates to 400 posts of veterinary officers.
The court observed that, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the cases, it was not appropriate to permit the investigation to continue either with the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) or the jurisdictional police, but it was equally not convinced that entrusting the probe to the CBI was the only available course.
Meanwhile, the court has named IPS officers Divya V. Gopinath, Anoop A. Shetty, Kushal Choksey, and Kshama Mishra as other members of the SIT.
The court also directed the State government to issue a notification declaring this SIT to be a police station for the purposes of investigation.
Independent and impartial
“The SIT shall conduct the investigation independently, impartially and uninfluenced by any observation made in this order on the merits of the allegations,” the court said.
The court also made it clear that the investigation by the SIT shall not be confined by the persons presently named, the allegations presently made or the contours presently perceived. “If the evidence gathered during investigation reveals involvement of any other person, offence, transaction or act, having a nexus with the subject matter of investigation, the SIT shall follow the evidence wherever it leads, strictly in accordance with law,” the court said.
The court gave liberty to the SIT to use the services of forensic, cyber, financial, technical or other specialised assistance for an effective investigation.
The court said that the SIT should extend cooperation to the Enforcement Directorate (ED), which has re has taken up probe under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, and receive information from ED.
KPSC’s troubled history
Tracing the “troubled history” of KPSC recruitments since 1998, the court noted that history reveals allegations recurring with disquieting similarity such as nepotism, favouritism, fraud, corruption, tampering of OMR sheets and even allegations of answers being written for candidates elsewhere, while the examination was under way.
“History, it is said, should teach institutions. It cannot be permitted merely to repeat itself, recruitment after recruitment, at the cost of thousands of aspirants whose only capital is merit and whose only expectation is fairness,” the court observed.
Pointing out that thousands of young men and women spend the most productive years of their lives preparing for these examinations believing that merit will ultimately have its day, the court said that when a post is sold, an OMR sheet is tampered with, marks are manipulated or a selection is engineered, merit is not merely defeated; it is betrayed.”
Such betrayal, the court said, “breeds cynicism among the young and creates the dangerous perception that constitutional avenues themselves are available for purchase. A recruitment scam in a Public Service Commission in particular is not merely a theft of post; it is a theft of equality of opportunity.”

briefs.headline: Karnataka launches action plan to cut salt intake by 30% by 2030
briefs.deck: The plan focuses on reducing salt consumption at three levels: households, food consumed outside the home, and processed and packaged foods.
briefs.bodyText:
Karnataka on Tuesday (September 22) launched a State action plan aimed at reducing population salt intake by 30% by 2030 and promoting healthier dietary habits as part of efforts to prevent non-communicable diseases (NCDs).
The Karnataka State Multisectoral Action Plan for Salt Reduction and Promotion of Healthy Dietary Habits focuses on reducing salt consumption at three levels — households, food consumed outside the home, and processed and packaged foods. It also seeks to encourage healthier food choices and strengthen dietary counselling through the health system.
The plan proposes measures to reduce the use of discretionary salt, encourage food manufacturers to reduce salt in processed and packaged foods, and promote awareness of healthier diets. It also envisages strengthening research and evidence on potassium-enriched low-sodium salt.
The action plan seeks to align Karnataka’s efforts with India’s commitment to the global target of reducing population salt intake by 30% by 2030, while encouraging progress towards the World Health Organisation (WHO) recommendation of less than five grams of salt per person per day.
TAG meeting
Health Minister U.T. Khader launched the plan at a Technical Advisory Group (TAG) meeting at Vidhana Soudha. Former Health Minister Dinesh Gundu Rao and Rajya Sabha member Mansoor Ali Khan were present.
The TAG was constituted under the chairpersonship of Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) Vice-Chancellor Bhagavan B.C. to provide technical guidance and support evidence-based action on salt reduction and healthier dietary practices.
The TAG brings together experts and representatives from the State Health department, Sri Jayadeva Institute of Cardiovascular Sciences and Research, NIMHANS, academic and nutrition institutions, and public health organisations including the Institute of Public Health (IPH), Resolve to Save Lives and Vision for Social Development.
The Minister said the plan would build on existing initiatives, including salt-reduction measures under PM POSHAN, dietary counselling through Gruha Arogya and dietary risk-factor counselling under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD).
State steering committee
Mr. Khader called for a State Steering Committee involving multiple departments to ensure coordinated and sustained action on healthier diets. Karnataka has already introduced measures addressing foods high in fat, sugar and salt, providing a basis for strengthening healthier food environments, the government said.
Jayadeva institute director Dinesha B. participated in the technical deliberations and stressed the need for coordinated action to address dietary risk factors.
Jnanesh Kamath, State Joint Director, presented the key priorities, objectives and proposed actions under the State plan. Raghunandan, State Deputy Director - Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD), Amrut Kadam of RGUHS; U.S. Vishal Rao, member of the Consultative Group to the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India; Syed Imran Farooq, Executive Director, and Manika Sharma, Principal Advisor, Food Policy, Resolve to Save Lives; and Amit Karnik, Director, Vision for Social Development, were among those present.

stories.headline: India begins anti-dumping probes against imports of Glycine chemical from China
stories.deck: If it is established that the dumping has caused material injury to domestic players, the DGTR would recommend the imposition of duties on the imports. The Finance Ministry takes the final decision to impose these duties
stories.bodyText:
India has initiated anti-dumping probes against imports of Glycine — used as a flavour enhancer and pharmaceutical ingredient from China — following a complaint filled by a domestic manufacturer.
The application was filled by Avid Organics before the Commerce Ministry's Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) to initiate the probe.
The applicant has alleged that the dumped imports from China are causing material injury to it. It has requested the imposition of anti-dumping duty on the imports, according to a DGTR notification.
For the probe, the directorate will consider the data between 2022-25. "The authority, hereby, initiates an antidumping investigation to determine the existence, degree, and effect of the dumping," it said on Tuesday (September 22, 2026).
If it is established that the dumping has caused material injury to domestic players, the DGTR would recommend the imposition of duties on the imports. The Finance Ministry takes the final decision to impose these duties.
U.S.-China trade tensions and China's significant industrial overcapacity pose a major risk of cheap Chinese goods being dumped in India.
In the recent period, India has initiated multiple such probes against dumped import of certain goods from China.
Anti-dumping probes are conducted by countries to determine if domestic industries have been hurt because of a surge in cheap imports. As a countermeasure, they impose these duties under the multilateral regime of the Geneva-based World Trade Organisation (WTO). The duty is aimed at ensuring fair trading practices and creating a level-playing field for domestic producers vis-a-vis foreign producers and exporters.
India and China are members of the WTO. India has already imposed anti-dumping duties on several products to tackle cheap imports from various countries, including China.
India's exports to China rose 36.66% to $19.47 billion during the last fiscal year, while imports increased 16% to $131.63 billion. The trade deficit swelled to an all-time high of $112.6 billion in 2025-26 as against $99.2 billion in 2024-25.
Anti-circumvention probe
In another notification, the DGTR said that it has started an investigation into allegations that anti-dumping duties on CPVC (Chlorinated Polyvinyl Chloride) resin from China and South Korea are being avoided by routing the product through Malaysia, Japan and Thailand.
The product is used in many industrial piping applications.
DCW Ltd, Epigral Ltd and Lubrizol Advanced Materials India in an application have alleged that the anti-dumping duty imposed on imports of this resin from China and Korea is being circumvented through exports from Japan, Malaysia and Thailand.
According to the notification, there is a change in the pattern of trade wherein imports of this product from Japan, Malaysia and Thailand have increased to a significant level without any sufficient cause or economic justification, thereby undermining the remedial effects of the existing anti-dumping measure imposed on the imports from China.
On the basis of the duly substantiated application filed by the applicants, the authority has found prima facie evidence that the anti-dumping duty is being circumvented and that the imports involved are being dumped.
"Accordingly, the Authority hereby initiates an anti-circumvention investigation ...to determine the existence and effect of the alleged circumvention of the existing anti-dumping duty on the product under consideration...," it said.

stories.headline: Govt. brings smartphone screen protectors under Bureau of Indian Standards
stories.deck: The mandatory BIS certification will be effective from April 1, 2027
stories.bodyText:
The government has mandated compulsory Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) certification for smartphone screen protectors, requiring entities to secure regulatory approval before selling such products in India.
The move is expected to curb sales of low-quality smartphone screen protectors and help domestic manufacturers like Optiemus Infracom, which has started production in India.
"The provisions of Electronics and Information Technology Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order, 2021, shall apply to the goods or articles as specified in column 2 (Screen Protectors for smartphones), added to the schedule of the said order by virtue of this notification, for conforming to the corresponding Indian standard as specified in column 3 IS 19348:2025), with effect from 1st April, 2027," a notification dated September 21 said.
Smartphone screen protectors are the 66th item to be notified under the rule. Other items in the list include smartphones, laptops, mobile and laptop chargers, LED televisions, microwave ovens, printers, and set-top boxes, among others.
"The introduction of mandatory BIS standards for screen protectors marks an important milestone for the category and a welcome step towards building a quality-led, Made-in-India ecosystem.
"At Optiemus Infracom, we are building on our existing screen-protector manufacturing capabilities, with a planned additional capacity of 2 crore units, to meet emerging demand and contribute to the growth of the domestic ecosystem," Optiemus Infracom executive chairman Ashok Gupta said.
Optiemus has set up a production unit in Noida to manufacture tempered glass screen protectors using technology from U.S. material technology firm Corning and expects to start shipments from January 2027.
The company expects ₹1,800-2,000 crore revenue in the current financial year from its tempered glass screen protectors business.
Mobile device makers body ICEA chairman Pankaj Mohindroo said mandatory BIS certification from April 1, 2027, will protect consumers from sub-standard products while creating a level playing field for domestic manufacturers and global companies alike.
"With a market of over 500 million units a year, this move will catalyse a Rs 12,000–16,000 crore quality-driven industry, generate around 60,000 direct and indirect jobs and contribute an estimated Rs 2,000 crore in GST revenues. It will also strengthen India’s potential as a global manufacturing and export hub for screen protectors," he said.
The domestic market for tempered glass screen protectors is estimated at 400 million pieces with a retail value of ₹20,000 crore in 2025.
